intended_object: For an object X = (E/S) of Ell/B with N invertible on S, the S-scheme Z of points of naive exact order N on E (Katz–Mazur): the open and closed subscheme of the N-torsion E[N] where no proper-divisor multiple dx meets the zero section, viewed as a scheme over S. I inferred this from the docstring and the module documentation of NaiveExactOrder/Basic.lean.
explanation: The body is `Over.mk (ι ≫ E[N].hom)`, where ι is the inclusion of the open subscheme `naiveExactOrderOpens hN` into E[N]. The underlying set of that subscheme is `naiveExactOrderLocus`: the points of E[N] where, for each divisor d ≠ N of N, the d-th multiple of the inclusion E[N] → E does not agree with the zero section. This is the Katz–Mazur naive exact order condition. The library proves the locus is open and closed when N is invertible on S, and that the subscheme represents the functor of points of naive exact order N (`naiveExactOrderRepresentableBy`). So the definition gives exactly the S-scheme Z → E[N] → S. Requiring N to be invertible is the standard hypothesis for the naive notion and is what makes the locus open, so it is not a needless restriction. The definition is a thin `EllObj` wrapper around the library's general construction for any elliptic curve over any scheme. Mathlib has no elliptic curves over schemes or torsion subschemes, so there is no broader counterpart.
